title: Pointwise exact locally closed extension
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), and $f:S\hookrightarrow X$ a locally closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Choose arbitrary commutative coefficient sheaves $R,R_S$ on the respective small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with a specified inverse-image identification $f^{-1}R\cong R_S$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use actual tensor pullback $f^*$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. There is an additive functor $F:\operatorname{Mod}(S,R_S)\to\operatorname{Mod}(X,R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] preserving finite limits and finite colimits, and an isomorphism $f^*F\cong1$. The construction is closed direct image followed by open extension by zero, with the composite coefficient identification [def-weil-pbc-strict-tower-operations] transported to the prescribed one. No adjunction for this composite extension is asserted. This extension is fully faithful on module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open; Tags 09AA, 09BM and 09BN. Coefficient and adjunction transport use sites-modules.tex Tags 03DI and 03DJ and categories.tex Tag 0037. This is a composite consequence in the specified sheaf-of-modules presentation.

proof.text: Factor the locally closed immersion as closed c followed by open v. Give V the inverse-image coefficient ring and c the inverse composite comparison followed by the prescribed coefficient identification. The composite coefficient identification is the prescribed one by isomorphism cancellation.

The source V of v is a subspace of the Noetherian space X. Its opens are Noetherian and therefore quasi-compact, so v and the complement of c are quasi-compact morphisms. The complement of v is realized by the subscheme of its vanishing ideal.

Apply identified-coefficient open/closed extension to v and its closed complement, obtaining exact additive open extension O and an adjunction O to v^* with invertible unit. Apply the same theorem to c and its open complement to obtain exact direct image c_* with invertible specified counit.

Take F=c_* followed by O. Finite limit and colimit preservation compose; finite biproduct preservation gives additivity of c_*. Whisker the specified composition comparison (vc)^* to c^*v^* by F, reassociate, then apply the inverse open unit and closed counit. This gives (vc)^*F isomorphic to the identity. The open unit and closed counit make their respective extension factors fully faithful. Their composite is therefore fully faithful on module sheaves.

lean.statement:
theorem proEtaleLocallyClosedExtension
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (f : S ⟶ X) [IsImmersion f]
    (R : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (Rs : Sheaf (ProEt.topology S) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (cf : (proEtaleSheafInverseImage f CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R ≅ Rs) :
    ∃ F : proEtaleRingModules S Rs ⥤ proEtaleRingModules X R,
      F.Additive ∧ PreservesFiniteLimits F ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits F ∧
        F.Full ∧ F.Faithful ∧
        Nonempty (F ⋙ proEtaleRingModulePullback f R Rs cf ≅ 𝟭 _)
